explanation: The German spring offensives of 1918 were made possible by the end of the eastern war: the armistice of December 1917 and the treaty of March 1918 released some fifty divisions for the west, and Ludendorff spent them on a run of attacks begun before American strength could arrive. Operation Georgette, which fell on the Lys on 9 April, was the second of them. The claim is about why an attack of that weight was available in that sector in that month, not about why the Portuguese 2nd Division broke under it — the state of the division is argued on the Portuguese record and is not settled here.
